title: Ankhorage DynamoDB Adapter
summary: Implements the portable Ankhorage database adapter contract with Amazon DynamoDB.
purpose: Expose explicitly bounded DynamoDB persistence through the provider-neutral database contract without leaking AWS request shapes to consumers.
responsibilities: Translate portable select, find, insert, update, and delete operations into DynamoDB document commands.
Map logical collections to explicitly configured tables, physical keys, and optional query indexes.
Normalize provider and validation failures into safe portable database errors.
Manage the lifecycle only of AWS clients created by the adapter.
boundaries: Does not provision DynamoDB tables, indexes, IAM policy, or AWS infrastructure.
Does not emulate relational joins, schemas, transactions, offset pagination, or arbitrary scans.
Does not own caller-provided AWS clients.
audience: Applications that require DynamoDB through the portable Ankhorage database contract.
Infrastructure adapters that supply explicit DynamoDB table and client configuration.
useCases: Query a bounded DynamoDB partition or configured secondary index.
Read, insert, update, or delete records by their configured physical keys.
Use a caller-owned client or let the adapter own and close its AWS client.

architecture.role: Provider adapter translating the portable DbAdapter boundary to AWS DynamoDB document operations.
invariants: Every operation resolves through an explicit logical-table mapping.
Writes cannot silently change configured physical key attributes.
Unsupported DynamoDB representations fail explicitly instead of simulating relational behavior.

configuration: Requires a non-empty mapping from logical collection names to DynamoDB tables and physical keys.
security: Provider error payloads, metadata, tokens, and stacks are not retained in portable results.
limitations: Transactions and realtime subscriptions are not supported.
Queries require a finite limit and reject results that need a continuation cursor.
Multi-item inserts, offset pagination, column projection, and schema-qualified tables are unsupported.
